raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup` is unset, a PD decode server resolves it (`kv_cache_builder.resolve_decode_retraction_backup`) to `host_pool` whenever the KV pool supports it. That builds a HiCache host pool. The host pool picks its allocator from `pool_host.common.ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS` by device type. Only `npu`, `musa` and `xpu` have entries, and every other device falls back to `alloc_with_host_register`, i.e. `cudaHostRegister`. On a device that is neither CUDA nor ROCm the server therefore crashes at startup, just because the user didn't pass a flag. That includes CPU and out-of-tree platforms such as Neuron/Trainium.

## Modifications

- New `kv_cache_builder.device_can_back_host_pool(device)`. It is True when the device type has an explicit host allocator in `ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS`, or when it is a CUDA/ROCm device. It checks keys with `in`, so it doesn't insert defaultdict entries.
- `resolve_decode_retraction_backup` only defaults to `host_pool` when that is true. Otherwise it defaults to `cpu_tensor`, the existing fallback used for HIP, DCP, recurrent-state models, etc.
- An explicit `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup host_pool` is unchanged and still honored.

## How it was found

Found bringing up PD on an out-of-tree Neuron/Trainium platform plugin. The decode server crashed in `cudaHostRegister` while building the backup-only host pool. The plugin currently works around it by setting `disaggregation_decode_retraction_backup = "cpu_tensor"` in its `apply_server_args_defaults`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. There is no change on CUDA/NPU/MUSA/XPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

- Run (macOS, CPU only): `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_retraction_backup_platform_default.py` (new). It checks that devices with a host allocator return True, that `cuda` returns True only on CUDA/ROCm builds, that CPU and unknown out-of-tree devices return False, and that the check doesn't mutate `ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS`.
- Not run: `test_decode_retraction_backup.py` is a CUDA test and cannot run here. No GPU PD e2e. The full `resolve_decode_retraction_backup` was not exercised end to end on CPU.

## Open questions

- Should this be a platform hook instead, e.g. `SRTPlatform.supports_host_memory_registration()` or a platform-provided host allocator? Then an out-of-tree platform could opt in to `host_pool` with its own pinned allocator, instead of inserting into `ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS`. I kept the device-type check because it matches how the allocator is chosen today.
- HiCache itself (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`) on such devices has the same `cudaHostRegister` fallback. Not addressed here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -26,6 +26,8 @@ class KVCacheBuildResult:
 
 from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
 
+import torch
+
 from sglang.srt.configs.hybrid_arch import (
     glm5_next_config,
     hybrid_gdn_config,
@@ -58,7 +60,7 @@ class KVCacheBuildResult:
     get_schedule,
 )
 from sglang.srt.speculative.base_spec_worker import HiCacheDraftMode
-from sglang.srt.utils import ceil_align, is_hip, is_npu
+from sglang.srt.utils import ceil_align, is_cuda, is_hip, is_npu
 
 if TYPE_CHECKING:
     from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig
@@ -183,6 +185,24 @@ def uses_ssm_state(model_config) -> bool:
     )
 
 
+def device_can_back_host_pool(device) -> bool:
+    """Whether the HiCache host pool can allocate pinned buffers for ``device``.
+
+    Devices without an entry in ``ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS`` fall back to
+    ``cudaHostRegister``, which only works on CUDA/ROCm. Elsewhere (CPU, and
+    out-of-tree devices that register no allocator) a host pool fails at
+    startup, so the default retraction backup must not pick it.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.common import ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS
+
+    device_type = device.type if isinstance(device, torch.device) else str(device)
+    device_type = device_type.split(":", 1)[0]
+    # ``in`` checks the explicit keys without creating a defaultdict entry.
+    if device_type in ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS:
+        return True
+    return device_type == "cuda" and (is_cuda() or is_hip())
+
+
 def resolve_decode_retraction_backup(*, tp_worker: BaseTpWorker) -> str:
     """Resolve the retraction backend onto the config bags and return it.
 
@@ -231,6 +251,7 @@ def resolve_decode_retraction_backup(*, tp_worker: BaseTpWorker) -> str:
             # Large ROCm retraction restores can fault the GPU process. Keep
             # host_pool opt-in on HIP until the retraction path is safe at scale.
             and not is_hip()
+            and device_can_back_host_pool(tp_worker.model_runner.device)
             and not get_parallel().dcp_enabled
             and not disagg.disaggregation_decode_enable_radix_cache
             # KV offload already owns a host pool; a second one double-books host memory.

@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+"""CPU tests: the default decode retraction backup only picks host_pool where
+the HiCache host pool can allocate its pinned buffers."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache import kv_cache_builder
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.common import ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+class TestDeviceCanBackHostPool(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_devices_with_a_host_allocator(self):
+        for device in ("npu", "musa", "xpu", "npu:0", torch.device("xpu", 1)):
+            with self.subTest(device=device):
+                self.assertTrue(kv_cache_builder.device_can_back_host_pool(device))
+
+    def test_cuda_registers_only_on_cuda_or_rocm(self):
+        with patch.object(kv_cache_builder, "is_cuda", return_value=True):
+            self.assertTrue(kv_cache_builder.device_can_back_host_pool("cuda"))
+            self.assertTrue(kv_cache_builder.device_can_back_host_pool("cuda:3"))
+        with (
+            patch.object(kv_cache_builder, "is_cuda", return_value=False),
+            patch.object(kv_cache_builder, "is_hip", return_value=False),
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(kv_cache_builder.device_can_back_host_pool("cuda"))
+
+    def test_cpu_and_out_of_tree_devices_fall_back(self):
+        for device in ("cpu", "neuron", "my_oot_device:0"):
+            with self.subTest(device=device):
+                self.assertFalse(kv_cache_builder.device_can_back_host_pool(device))
+        self.assertNotIn("neuron", ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS, "query must not insert keys")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
